examples.en: I sprayed hairspray on my hair.
This spray smells nice.
I painted a picture on the wall with spray paint.
There is a mosquito spray in my bag.
The tip of the spray is clogged, so nothing comes out.

examples.ko: 여행 갈 때 작은 스프레이도 챙겼어요.
examples.en: I packed a small spray bottle for the trip too.

explain: 분무기처럼 뿜어 나오는 액체 전체에 써요. 머리에 쓰면 '헤어스프레이', 벌레를 쫓으면 '모기 스프레이'처럼 쓰임을 앞에 붙여서 불러요. 뿌릴 때는 '뿌리다'를 써요.
explain_en: It covers any liquid that comes out in a mist. The use goes in front: 헤어스프레이 for hair, 모기 스프레이 for keeping mosquitoes away. To spray it, use 뿌리다.

examples.en: I let the steam out of the pressure cooker and opened the lid.

examples.ko: 압력솥으로 밥을 하면 훨씬 빨리 돼요.
examples.en: Cooking rice in a pressure cooker is much faster.
The pressure cooker started making a hissing sound.
If you make braised ribs in a pressure cooker, the meat gets tender.
My mother boiled potatoes in the pressure cooker.

examples.ko: 압력솥 뚜껑이 안 열려서 한참 기다렸어요.
examples.en: The pressure cooker lid wouldn't open, so I waited a long time.

explain: '밥솥'은 밥을 짓는 솥이고, '압력솥'은 압력으로 음식을 빨리 익히는 솥이라 찜이나 삶는 요리에도 써요. '김'은 뜨거운 수증기를 뜻해서 '김이 나다', '김을 빼다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: A '밥솥' is a pot for cooking rice, while a '압력솥' cooks food quickly under pressure, so it is also used for braising and boiling. Here '김' means hot steam, as in '김이 나다' (steam comes out) and '김을 빼다' (let the steam out).

examples.en: The children are playing ball in the front yard.
There is a persimmon tree in the front yard of my grandmother's house.
When spring comes, we plant flowers in the front yard.
I feel refreshed after sweeping the front yard.
The puppy runs around happily in the front yard.
We made a small vegetable patch in the front yard of our house.

explain: 집 앞쪽에 있는 뜰이고, 반대말은 '뒤뜰'이에요. 단독 주택이나 시골집 이야기에서 주로 나오고, 일반적으로 집 앞 공간은 '마당'이라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is the garden in front of a house, and the opposite is '뒤뜰' (backyard). It mostly appears when talking about detached houses or country homes, and the open space in front of a house is also generally called '마당'.

examples.en: I recycled old clothes into a bag.
Plastic can only be recycled if you sort it.
This paper cup is hard to recycle.
Don't throw the bottle away; try reusing it.
Our shop reuses packaging boxes.
The souvenir is a bag made of recycled fabric.

explain: '재활용품', '재활용 쓰레기', '재활용 센터'처럼 앞말로도 많이 써요. 쓰레기를 종류별로 나눠 버리는 건 '분리수거'라고 해요. 일상에서는 '다시 쓰다'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: It is often used before another noun, as in '재활용품', '재활용 쓰레기' and '재활용 센터'. Sorting trash by type is called '분리수거'. In daily talk people also say '다시 쓰다'.

examples.en: I listen to music with headphones on the subway.

examples.ko: 새 헤드폰을 사고 싶어서 가격을 비교하고 있어요.
examples.en: I want to buy new headphones, so I am comparing prices.
The headphones fit tightly on my ears and hurt.
I put my headphones in my bag so I do not lose them.

examples.ko: 이 헤드폰 정말 가볍고 소리도 선명해요.
examples.en: These headphones are really light and the sound is clear.
I made a call with the microphone on the headphones.

explain: '이어폰'은 귀에 꽂고 헤드폰은 머리에 걸쳐요. 헤드폰은 '끼다'와 '쓰다'를 모두 써요.
explain_en: 이어폰 goes into your ears, while 헤드폰 sits over your head. For wearing headphones, both 끼다 and 쓰다 are used.
